## Pull request overview

Aligns ObjectUI’s UI-facing schema/types and SpecBridge transforms with `@objectstack/spec` v3.0.8 (P1 roadmap items), and adds/updates tests to validate the expanded protocol surface.

**Changes:**
- Added new/expanded schema types (record component props, ListView/ObjectGrid additions, expanded PageType/PageSchema, Dashboard enhancements) and re-exported spec UI types under `Spec*` names.
- Updated SpecBridge bridges (list-view/form-view/page/dashboard) to pass through new spec properties into `SchemaNode`.
- Added P1-focused test suites for types and SpecBridge; updated ROADMAP.md completion checkboxes and metrics.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 12 out of 12 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/types/src/record-components.ts | New record:* component prop interfaces (spec-aligned). |
| packages/types/src/objectql.ts | Adds P1.1 ListView props + ObjectGrid spec-aligned props (conditional formatting, virtual scroll, actions, emptyState). |
| packages/types/src/layout.ts | Expands `PageType`, extends `PageVariable`, adds `blankLayout`, adds Page ARIA block. |
| packages/types/src/index.ts | Exports new record component types + re-exports spec UI types with `Spec*` prefixes. |
| packages/types/src/complex.ts | Extends Dashboard/DashboardWidget schemas with P1.3 fields (binding, header, filters, dateRange, aria). |
| packages/types/src/__tests__/p1-spec-alignment.test.ts | New type-level tests covering P1 additions across schemas. |
| packages/react/src/spec-bridge/bridges/page.ts | Page bridge now forwards description/icon/blankLayout/width/variables/source/aria/etc. |
| packages/react/src/spec-bridge/bridges/list-view.ts | ListView bridge forwards new P1.1 + P1.6 props. |
| packages/react/src/spec-bridge/bridges/form-view.ts | FormView bridge maps `type → formType` + forwards defaultSort/sharing/aria. |
| packages/react/src/spec-bridge/bridges/dashboard.ts | Dashboard bridge forwards P1.3 fields (header/globalFilters/dateRange/aria/etc). |
| packages/react/src/spec-bridge/__tests__/P1SpecBridge.test.ts | New bridge tests validating passthrough/mapping for P1. |
| ROADMAP.md | Marks P1 items completed; updates test-count/protocol-alignment metrics. |
</details>



<details>
<summary>Comments suppressed due to low confidence (6)</summary>

**packages/types/src/objectql.ts:464**
* `ObjectGridSchema.conditionalFormatting` is documented as aligned with `ListViewSchema.conditionalFormatting`, but `ListViewSchema` uses a different rule shape (`field`/`operator`/`value`/`expression?`). This creates two incompatible contracts under the same name. Consider reusing a shared rule type (or renaming one of the properties) and update the comment to reflect the actual expected format.
```
    /** Expression-based condition (e.g., '${data.amount > 1000}') */
    condition: string;
    /** Style map (e.g., { backgroundColor: '#fee2e2', textColor: '#991b1b' }) */
    style: Record<string, string>;
  }>;
```
**packages/react/src/spec-bridge/bridges/list-view.ts:59**
* `ListViewSpec.aria` is treated as a nested object and passed through as `node.aria`. That doesn’t integrate with `SchemaRenderer`’s ARIA injection (top-level `ariaLabel`/`ariaDescribedBy`/`role`) and can cause invalid DOM attributes if a downstream renderer spreads props. Prefer flattening ARIA onto the node’s top-level fields instead of passing an `aria` object through.
```
  // P1.6 i18n & ARIA
  aria?: { ariaLabel?: string; ariaDescribedBy?: string; role?: string };
  sharing?: any;
```
**packages/react/src/spec-bridge/__tests__/P1SpecBridge.test.ts:124**
* This test asserts a nested `aria` object on the transformed node (`node.aria.ariaLabel`). Runtime ARIA injection in `SchemaRenderer` is driven by top-level `ariaLabel`/`ariaDescribedBy`/`role`, so the bridge/tests should ideally validate the flattened fields (or add a render-level assertion that `aria-label` appears in the DOM).
```
        aria: { ariaLabel: 'Accounts List', role: 'grid' },
      });

      expect(node.aria).toBeDefined();
      expect(node.aria.ariaLabel).toBe('Accounts List');
```
**packages/types/src/__tests__/p1-spec-alignment.test.ts:515**
* This test validates ARIA as a nested `aria` object on `DashboardSchema`, but runtime ARIA injection expects top-level `ariaLabel`/`ariaDescribedBy`/`role`. As written, the test can pass while accessibility is still broken. Consider asserting the flattened fields (or adding a small render test that verifies `aria-label` ends up on the DOM).
```
      aria: {
        ariaLabel: 'Sales Dashboard',
        role: 'region',
      },
    };
```
**packages/types/src/objectql.ts:477**
* Spec-aligned actions are added as `rowSpecActions` here, but the SpecBridge currently maps spec `rowActions` onto `node.rowActions` (which already exists on `ObjectGridSchema` with ObjectUI-specific semantics). Consider aligning naming end-to-end (either migrate `rowActions` to the spec meaning or map into `rowSpecActions`/`bulkSpecActions` and ensure renderers consume those).
```
  /**
   * Row action identifiers (action names from ActionSchema).
   * Aligned with @objectstack/spec ListViewSchema.rowActions.
   */
  rowSpecActions?: string[];
```
**packages/react/src/spec-bridge/bridges/form-view.ts:107**
* `FormViewSpec.aria` is passed through as `node.aria`, but ARIA injection expects top-level fields. This risks being a no-op for accessibility and can become a DOM attribute issue if a renderer spreads props. Prefer mapping `spec.aria.*` onto top-level `ariaLabel`/`ariaDescribedBy`/`role` on the returned node.
```
  // P1.6 — i18n & ARIA
  if (spec.sharing) node.sharing = spec.sharing;
  if (spec.aria) node.aria = spec.aria;

```
</details>

`PageSpec.aria` is modeled as a nested object. Downstream, `SchemaRenderer`’s ARIA injection is based on top-level `ariaLabel`/`ariaDescribedBy`/`role`, so passing a raw `aria` object through tends to be a no-op (or becomes an invalid DOM attribute if spread). Prefer flattening ARIA onto the output node’s top-level fields.

`PageSchema` introduces a nested `aria` object, but the runtime ARIA injection is based on top-level `ariaLabel`/`ariaDescribedBy`/`role` (see `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:33-44`). With the current shape, `PageRenderer` will receive an `aria` prop and spread it onto a DOM `<div>`, which can render an invalid `aria="[object Object]"` attribute and still not set `aria-label`. Prefer flattening these fields onto the schema (or explicitly consume `schema.aria.*` in `PageRenderer` and do not spread the raw object).
```suggestion
   * Accessible name for the page container.
   * Mapped to the DOM `aria-label` attribute.
   */
  ariaLabel?: string;
  /**
   * ID reference to element(s) that describe the page.
   * Mapped to the DOM `aria-describedby` attribute.
   */
  ariaDescribedBy?: string;
  /**
   * Landmark or widget role for the page root container.
   * Mapped to the DOM `role` attribute.
   */
  role?: string;
```

`spec.aria` is assigned to `node.aria`, but the renderer only injects ARIA attributes from top-level `ariaLabel`/`ariaDescribedBy`/`role`. Since `PageRenderer` spreads unknown props onto its root `<div>`, this risks emitting an invalid `aria="[object Object]"` attribute and still not setting `aria-label`. Map `spec.aria.*` onto top-level fields and avoid passing a raw `aria` object through.
